text:
MPC rose 0.83% today to close at $458.81, continuing a strong two-week rally that has pushed the stock up 17.81% since early October. The immediate driver is the sharp rebound in oil prices: Brent crude topped $106 this past week after the Saudi airport attack, and with refineries running at 92.7% capacity and diesel inventories relatively tight at 105 million barrels, a refiner like Marathon profits when crude prices rise and refining margins widen. Even though oil prices have pulled back slightly today as traders weigh Russian diesel supply prospects against Middle East tensions, the underlying environment for U.S. refiners remains supportive—global oil at $125 per barrel versus U.S. oil at $96 suggests healthy refining spreads.

The broader context is geopolitical: Iran's nuclear fortification, the Saudi-Houthi conflict, and uncertainty over Trump's Russian diesel deal have kept energy markets volatile and elevated. Refiners benefit from this uncertainty because it keeps crude prices firm and creates margin opportunities, even if the long-term policy picture around sanctions remains unsettled.
